title: Shared pairs in dinitrogen
statement:
How many shared electron pairs connect the nitrogen atoms in the usual Lewis structure of N₂?

[_]{a}

explanations: A triple bond contains three pairs and each N keeps one lone pair.
A single bond would not complete both octets with ten electrons.
Two pairs would still leave the standard octets incomplete.
Five shared pairs would exceed the nitrogen octet.

hints: Each nitrogen supplies five valence electrons.
Two remaining electrons stay on each nitrogen.
solution: Each nitrogen supplies five valence electrons. Both need eight around them. Two remaining electrons stay on each nitrogen. A triple bond contains three pairs and each N keeps one lone pair.
